catalog_citation: Li, Paul Jen-kuei. 1991. Vowel deletion and vowel assimilation in Sediq. In Robert Blust (ed.), Currents in Pacific Linguistics: papers on Austronesian languages and ethnolinguistics in honour of George W. Grace (Pacific Linguistics C-117), 163-169. Canberra:…
catalog_locator: p.165, prose under rule (7a) 'Vowel deletion before stress' (PDF page 3 of sealang)
catalog_quote: Stress mostly falls on the penultimate syllable of the word in all Sediq dialects. All word-initial vowels get deleted, as illustrated in (7b). Any other vowel before a true consonant that is immediately followed by the stressed vowel, and all vowels between consonants before a stressed syllable are reduced to a phonetic [u] or [ə], depending on the dialect or speaker, as in (7c). ... It is clear from the above data that Sediq has a general vowel-deletion rule. Only stressed vowels retain their full vowel value, whereas vowels before stress either get deleted or reduced to a phonetic [u] (or [ə] in the other dialects).

new_statements.quote: 2.2.4 重音 霧社方言的重音，很規則的落在多音節詞的倒數第二音節，或是在單音節非語法詞語位的該音節上。例如：(43) maxan [máxan] 十 sulau [suláu] 梳子 (44) buc [búc] 骨 iq [íq] 表示不同意的回答 a [á] 感歎詞 可用規律表示為：(45) V → V́ / __(C)V(C)# (46) V → V́ / #(C)__(C)# 若是單音節的語法詞，則沒有重音，如 di, ge, sa 等。…一個語位，一旦加上後加成分，重音也會轉移到新詞的倒數第二音節。如：(47) 語幹 [qulúli] ~ 命令態 [qululí-i] 流 [tútiŋ] ~ [tutíŋ-i] 藏 因為重音是在多音節語位的倒數第二音節上，因此語位加上前加成分時，並不引起重音的轉移。…也就是說，重音不落在前加成分上。如：(48) [búc] 骨 [mu-gu-búc] 變成骨 [p.628:] 事實上，霧社方言並沒有長短元音的區別。雖然重音節的元音，感覺上比其它位置的元音要長，但是這種可預測的重音節長元音並不具辨義作用
new_statements.translation: 2.2.4 Stress. Stress in the Wushe (Paran) dialect falls very regularly on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic words, or on the single syllable of a monosyllabic non-grammatical (content) morpheme. E.g. (43) maxan [máxan] 'ten', sulau [suláu] 'comb'; (44) buc [búc] 'bone', iq [íq] 'answer expressing disagreement', a [á] interjection. As rules: (45) V -> stressed / __(C)V(C)#; (46) V -> stressed / #(C)__(C)#. Monosyllabic grammatical words have no stress, e.g. di, ge, sa. ... Once a suffix is added to a morpheme, the stress shifts to the penultimate syllable of the new word, e.g. (47) stem [qulúli] ~ imperative [qululí-i] 'flow', [tútiŋ] ~ [tutíŋ-i] 'hide'. Because stress is on the penult of a polysyllabic morpheme, adding a prefix causes no stress shift ... that is, stress never falls on a prefix, e.g. (48) [búc] 'bone', [mu-gu-búc] 'become bone'. [p.628:] In fact the Wushe dialect has no long/short vowel distinction; although the vowel of the stressed syllable feels longer than vowels elsewhere, this predictable stressed-syllable length is not distinctive.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penult: penultimate stress); adds the formal rule, the treatment of monosyllables (content words stressed, function words unstressed), stress shift under suffixation, the no-stress-on-prefixes clause yielding final stress on prefixed monosyllabic stems, and the remark that stressed-vowel lengthening is non-distinctive.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fully predictable: it falls on the penultimate syllable of any polysyllabic word (rule V -> V́ / __(C)V(C)#); monosyllabic content words are stressed on their only syllable; monosyllabic grammatical/function words (di, ge, sa) are unstressed. Suffixation shifts stress rightward to the new penult ([qulúli] ~ [qululí-i]); prefixes never bear stress, so a prefixed monosyllabic stem keeps final stress ([mu-gu-búc]). Stressed vowels are phonetically somewhat longer, but length is non-contrastive. The author notes (p.620) that stress is so regular on the penult that word-final voiceless echo vowels after h are left out of the phonemic transcription to avoid confusing the stress count.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic grammatical words (di, ge, sa etc.) carry no stress; prefixed monosyllabic stems surface with final stress because prefixes are never stressed ([mu-gu-búc] 'become bone'); word-final non-syllabic echo vowels after h do not count as syllables for stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes the Paran dialect of Seediq (霧社方言, self-designation Paran; = Tgdaya), as spoken in Nanfeng 南豐 and Huzhu 互助 villages, Ren'ai township, Nantou county (fieldwork 1974-1976, main consultants from Nanfeng). The author notes other Seediq dialects (e.g. Truku/Toda areas in Hualien and other Ren'ai villages) exist and differ lexically (seedaq vs sediq/sazi?) but the description is confined to Paran. Glottocode taro1264 covers Seediq/Taroko as a whole, so this is a dialect-level source for the same language.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation is verbatim on p.165 (p.3) of the Li 1991 PDF we hold, at the stated locator. (2) The classification (fixed penultimate, weight-blind, suffixes re-penultimise, pretonic reduction/deletion) rests on a 1991 phonology article by Paul Li whose stress line is a premise; but it is independently and explicitly confirmed by three first-hand grammars, one already held (Ochiai 2016 Kyoto PhD, §2.2 p.14: penultimate 'without exception' in Paran; clitics unstressed; loans penult; §6.6.1 p.114 suffix-driven shift) and two downloaded now from the open 原住民族委員會 ebooks (Song 2018 §2.3.2 p.18, Tgdaya: 'always penultimate', shifts under suffixation; Lee & Hsu 2018 §2.3.2 p.19, Truku: 'generally penultimate', shifts under suffixation). Oiwa-Bungard 2017 transcriptions agree. No source seen suggests anything but penultimate stress; the only refinements are Li's hedge 'mostly' vs Ochi

sources.quote: '在太魯閣語中，重音一般落在詞的倒數第二音節，如patas [pá.tas]「書」。加了-an、-un或-i等後綴的詞亦適用此一重音規則...例如ptasan /patas-an/ [pə.tá.san]' (In Truku, stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; suffixed words follow the same rule, pre-stress vowels weaken to schwa). Adds: the rule also applies when enclitics (bound pronouns, particle da) attach — patas mu [pa.tás.mu], mowsa ku da [mo.sa.kú.da] '重音落在詞組的倒數第二音節' (stress on the penult of the word+clitic group), but without vowel weakening; p.17/27: Truku allows a stressed schwa in the penult (hema [hə́.ma]).

sources.citation: Song, Limei 宋麗梅. 2018. 賽德克語語法概論 [An introduction to Seediq grammar], 2nd ed. (臺灣南島語言叢書 5). New Taipei: 原住民族委員會. ISBN 978-986-05-5686-5. (Tgdaya dialect)
sources.quote: '賽德克語重音都落在詞的倒數第二音節，故通常無須標示。當詞根或詞幹加上後詞綴時，重音亦跟著移動，使重音仍落在所成新詞的倒數第二音節上。' (Seediq stress always falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, so it normally need not be marked; when a suffix is added stress moves so that it still falls on the penult of the new word), ex. quyux [qú.yux] -> qyuxan [qu.yú.xan]; §2.3.3.1: vowels /i u e o a/ outside the stressed syllable neutralise to [u]; word-initial unstressed vowel deletes (eyah -> yahan [yá.han]).
